concerns.text: Task T023a implements a conditional Gaussian Process (GP) that only fits if Moran's I > 0.15. This violates Spec US-2 and Plan 'Constitution Check VII' which mandate a 'mandatory a priori' GP random effect. The task silently weakens the model specification by making the GP optional based on a diagnostic.

Tasks T005c1/T005c2 implement a fallback from NOAA/PRISM to Daymet. Spec FR-001 and Constitution Principle VI explicitly mandate 'NOAA PRISM' data. While the Plan notes a 'Critical Data Scope Note' allowing Daymet, the tasks do not explicitly document this as a sanctioned deviation in the task description itself, creating a silent drift from the constitutional requirement without a clear 'whitelisted deviation' flag in the task logic.

Task T031c includes a fallback to 'scipy.spatial.distance.geodesic' and 'numpy' if 'geomstats' is unavailable. Spec FR-006 and US-3 strictly require 'Riemannian manifold' statistics. A Euclidean/flat approximation fallback violates the strict Riemannian requirement, effectively weakening the core analytical method if the primary library is missing.

Task T023b (Moran's I) is a blocking dependency for T023a (GAMM fit). Spec US-2 and Plan Phase 2.2 define Moran's I as a 'post-hoc' diagnostic. Making the model fit dependent on a post-hoc diagnostic contradicts the 'a priori' model structure requirement and creates an incorrect workflow.

Task T043 references 'src/analysis/power_analysis.py' to satisfy SC-001 (Statistical Power) but this script is not defined in the task list (only mentioned as 'to be implemented'). This leaves the acceptance criterion for SC-001 unmeasurable and the requirement unfulfilled.
